# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: DECSCL select conformance level (CSI Pl ; Pc " p)  (issue #92, wave 6)
# crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/decscl_spec.txt   (implementer-written, lead decision D1:
# no spec-researcher run; xterm's CASE_DECSCL and decstr_spec.txt's D-DECSCL are the sources)
#
# Same machine-readable layout as decstr_spec.txt (### ID / size / step / cite / note / screen /
# cursor / pending_wrap / requests / scrollback), parsed by tests/spec/mod.rs `parse_fixture`.
# Extra keys the shared parser ignores and tests/decscl.rs asserts by hand:
#     pen:     Terminal::grid().pen() after the script: "default" or "not default"
#     cellpen: style of one cell, "(row,col)=default" or "(row,col)=fg=indexed(N)"
#     region:  grid.scroll_region(): "full" or "top..=bottom", 0-based
#     modes:   `field=bool` pairs for Terminal::modes(): origin, insert, auto_wrap, cursor_visible
#     level:   Terminal::conformance_level() (1..=5; 4 on a new terminal)
#     c1:      Terminal::c1_8bit_replies(): "7bit" (false) or "8bit" (true)
#     flags:   control | negative | deviation
# `control` cases run without DECSCL and prove a neighbour's setup really produces the state
# DECSCL resets; `negative` cases send a near miss (no level, a level outside 61..65, another
# intermediate or final, a colon sub-parameter) that must not reset anything or change the level.
# Every other case sends a valid DECSCL (`CSI 61..65 [; digits]* " p`); tests/decscl.rs checks that.
# Every case is run whole and byte by byte; every case expects `requests: []` (lead decision D3:
# DECSCL is silent).
#
# PRIMARY SOURCES
#   [CTL]  xterm ctlseqs  https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html  'CSI Pl ; Pc " p'
#          "Set conformance level (DECSCL), VT220 and up. Pl = 61 -> level 1, e.g., VT100 ...
#          Pl = 65 -> level 5, e.g., VT500. The second parameter selects the C1 control
#          transmission mode. This is an optional parameter, ignored in conformance level 1.
#          Pc = 0 -> 8-bit controls. Pc = 1 -> 7-bit controls (DEC factory default).
#          Pc = 2 -> 8-bit controls."
#   [XT]   xterm source (the oracle), ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots master, charproc.c
#          `case CASE_DECSCL:` (~L5088..5133):
#            if (terminal_id >= 200 && GetParam(0) >= 61 && GetParam(0) <= 60 + terminal_id/100) {
#                case_value = zero_if_default(1);        // absent Pc counts as 0
#                ReallyReset(xw, False, False);          // the DECSTR soft reset
#                init_parser(xw, sp);                    // REP's lastchar forgotten
#                set_vtXX_level(screen, GetParam(0) - 60);
#                if (new_vtXX_level > 1) switch (case_value) {
#                    case 1: show_8bit_control(False); break;
#                    case 0: case 2: show_8bit_control(True); break; }   // other Pc: unchanged
#            }
#            ResetState(sp);                             // anything else: no effect at all
#          The parse table (VTPrsTbl.c) routes `"` + `p` to CASE_DECSCL; no Request is answered.
#          RIS (ReallyReset full) calls show_8bit_control(False) and never touches vtXX_level
#          (it is set from decTerminalID once, at start-up).
#   [DEC]  VT510 RM DECSCL  https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DECSCL.html
#          "The factory default is level 4 (VT Level 4 mode, 7-bit controls)." Level 1 is
#          `CSI 61 " p`, "VT100 mode", with no Pc form (a VT100 has no 8-bit controls);
#          `CSI 6n " p` and `CSI 6n ; 0 " p` / `; 2` select 8-bit controls, `; 1` 7-bit.
#          "When you change the conformance level, the terminal performs a hard reset (RIS)."
#   [D-DECSCL] decstr_spec.txt header: "xterm's DECSCL (`CSI 61..64 ; Ps " p`) is itself a soft
#          reset (ReallyReset(soft) + level change) ... `CSI " p` (param 0 is not 61..64) does
#          nothing in xterm either" -- this fixture is that follow-up.
#
# DECISIONS (brief #92 "Done when", recorded here)
#   Soft, not hard: xterm (the oracle), the VT220 manual and DEC STD 070 reset softly; the
#     VT510 note says RIS. Follow xterm: screen, scrollback, cursor position and tab stops kept.
#   Level 65 accepted (flags: deviation): the brief accepts 61..65 with the default level 4.
#     xterm with its default decTerminalID 420 accepts only 61..64 (GetParam(0) <= 60 + 4) and
#     ignores 65; it accepts 65 only when started as a VT5xx.
#   Level 61 forces 7-bit replies (flags: deviation): the brief and DEC (VT100 mode has no
#     8-bit controls). xterm skips the Pc switch at level 1 and so keeps the previous mode.
#   Pc absent counts as 0 (8-bit), as xterm's zero_if_default(1) and DEC's `CSI 6n " p` form.
#     Pc 3 and up leave the mode as it was (xterm's switch has no default arm).
#   Parameters after Pc are ignored (xterm reads only GetParam(0) and GetParam(1)).
#   Colon sub-parameters: the whole sequence is ignored, like every non-SGR, non-XTMODKEYS
#     sequence (ADR 0020).
#   RIS keeps the level and turns 8-bit replies off (xterm ReallyReset full); DECSTR keeps both.
#
# Cursor is 0-based (row,col). render_screen puts `|` AFTER the cursor's cell.
# =============================================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ defaults

### DEFAULT01_new_terminal_is_level_4_7bit
size: 1x10
step: feed X
flags: control
cite: [DEC] "factory default is level 4 (VT Level 4 mode, 7-bit controls)"; [XT] set_vtXX_level(terminal_id / 100) with decTerminalID 420; [CTL] Pc = 1 "DEC factory default"
note: The starting point every other row changes. Nothing sent but a glyph.
screen:
>X |
cursor: (0,1)
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=0
level: 4
c1: 7bit

size: 1x10
step: feed \x1b[31m\x1b[61"p
step: feed X
cite: [CTL] Pl = 61 -> level 1, VT100; [XT] CASE_DECSCL ReallyReset(soft) then set_vtXX_level(1); [DEC] `CSI 61 " p` VT100 mode
note: The pen set before DECSCL is gone (soft reset ran), so X is in the default style; level 1, 7-bit.
screen:
>X |
cursor: (0,1)
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=0
pen: default
cellpen: (0,0)=default
level: 1
c1: 7bit

step: feed \x1b[62;2"p

step: feed X
flags: deviation
cite: [CTL] "ignored in conformance level 1"; [DEC] level 1 is VT100 mode (no 8-bit controls); brief #92 "Level 61 forces 7-bit replies regardless of Pc"; [XT] skips the switch at level 1 and would KEEP 8-bit here
note: Starts in 8-bit mode (`CSI 62 ; 2 " p`) so the forced 7-bit is visible: neither the Pc 2 nor the earlier 8-bit mode survives level 1. xterm deviates (keeps 8-bit); tessera follows DEC.
screen:

# ---------------------------------------------------- the reset really runs

### RESET01_pen_region_modes_reset
size: 4x10
step: feed ab\x1b[2;3r\x1b[?6h\x1b[31m\x1b[4h\x1b[?25lcd
step: feed \x1b[62;1"p
step: feed \x1b[1;1HX
cite: [XT] CASE_DECSCL -> ReallyReset(xw, False, False), the DECSTR path (decstr_spec.txt PEN01, IRM01, REGION01, DECOM01, TCEM01); [D-DECSCL]
note: After the reset DECOM is off, so CUP 1;1 is the screen's corner, and IRM is off, so X overwrites `a` (with IRM on the row would read `Xab`); X takes the default pen; the region is the full screen and the cursor visible again. `cd` keeps its red: the screen is not touched. RESET02 is the same script without DECSCL.
screen:
>Xb|
>cd
>
>
cursor: (0,1)
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=0
pen: default
cellpen: (0,0)=default
region: full
modes: origin=false insert=false auto_wrap=true cursor_visible=true
level: 2
c1: 7bit

### NEAR01_other_intermediates_finals_and_subparams
size: 4x10
step: feed ab\x1b[2;3r\x1b[?6h\x1b[31m\x1b[4h\x1b[?25lcd
step: feed \x1b[62:1"p\x1b[62"q\x1b[62$p\x1b[62'p\x1b[?62"p\x1b[62""p\x1b[62 p
step: feed \x1b[1;1HX
flags: negative
cite: [XT] `"` + `q` is DECSCA (#95), `$ p` DECRQM, `' p`, `? "` and `""` reach other or no cases; colon sub-parameters: ADR 0020 (xterm takes them only in SGR and XTMODKEYS)
note: None of these is DECSCL: the RESET02 state survives and the level stays 4. (DECRQM's reply is #10; nothing is answered today.)
screen:
>ab
>Xc|d
>
>
cursor: (1,1)
pending_wrap: false
